title: Access paths & fallback UX — org console wireframe notes
content:
Context:
Quick working notes from a short design pairing with SRE and Solutions on better surfacing of access paths, fallbacks, and quick remediation actions in the org/team settings console. Goal: reduce time-to-recovery when keys/roles are misconfigured and make safe defaults explicit. This is a sketch -> grooming doc, not final UX.

Problem statements we iterated on:
- Admins discover broken integrations only after customer impact; tracing who/what used a key is painful.
- API key rotation is conceptually simple but error-prone; current UI encourages manual copy/paste with no safe test path.
- Service accounts are overloaded: some are long-lived (automation), some ephemeral (deployments). Console mixes them.
- RBAC complexity: cross-team role inheritance and temporary delegation edges are opaque.
- Audit logs are dense and hard to filter by access path (api-key vs service-account vs org-role).

Design principles to hold:
- Make the common path simple (rotate key, create service account, add to team) while exposing advanced controls progressively.
- Provide inexpensive safety nets: live test (dry-run token), automatic fallback mapping, and clear revert.
- Surface ownership and last-used metadata prominently; show likely blast radius before an action.

Wireframe / component sketches (textual):
1) Access Path Overview (Org > Settings > Access Paths tab)
   - Top row: Org-level summary chips: active API keys (count), service accounts (count), users-with-admin (count), open-roles (custom).
   - Heatmap-style list for "recently used by" with small avatars + resource icons (api-key, svcacct, user). Hover shows last-used timestamp and the route (hosted vs dedicated).
   - Quick actions dropdown on each row: rotate, disable, create fallback, open audit trail.

2) Safe Rotate Modal (for API Keys & Service Account tokens)
   - Stepper: 1) Create replacement (auto-generated), 2) Dry-run / smoke test (button: run test with sample request), 3) Promote & schedule cutover, 4) Auto-expire old key (configurable: immediate, 1h, 24h, 7d).
   - Important: show "Potential impacted routes" list computed from routing policy (if a key is used by a route pinned to a model variant, show it).
   - Option: "Create automatic fallback" that will route calls using old key to a safe read-only variant for 24h if new key fails.

3) Fallbacks concept (new primitive)
   - A fallback is a short config mapping: {primary key/service-account -> fallback model/route OR user contact}.
   - UI: small inline card when creating rotation or service account change: "Add fallback" with suggestions (e.g., read-only model, admin-notify, dedicated-standby).
   - Allow toggling fallback activation manually from Access Path list. Show last fallback invocation time.

4) Compact Audit Timeline (inline for each access object)
   - Collapsible timeline: Show events grouped by day; key columns: event, actor (user/service), route, result (200/4xx/5xx), token used (masked but labelled: key-abc-*** or svc-123-ephemeral).
   - Filters above timeline: by actor, by token type, by outcome, by route, free-text. Saveable filter presets.
   - One-click "Open replay" to replay the event in a sandboxed replay runner (for debug, does not contact production resources).

5) Service Account Mode toggle (within svcacct create/edit)
   - Mode: Ephemeral (recommended for CI/CD) vs Long-lived (for infra tools).
   - Ephemeral flow: show steps to integrate with our short-lifetime token exchange endpoint and example IaC snippet.
   - Long-lived: require a justification field and optional scheduled rotation cadence with automated reminders.

6) Role Shadows & Delegation view
   - Visual graph: team nodes and roles. Shadowed permissions (when team A has permissions via team B) are highlighted. Clicking shows example API calls enabled by the shadow.
   - Delegation audit: list of temporary grants with expiry and the delegate owner. Provide easy revoke.

Open questions we flagged:
- How much of the fallback primitive should be machine-managed vs human? e.g., auto-failover to read-only vs. auto-swap to admin key. Security concerns need review (S1).
- Replay runner: how many event types are safe to replay and how to ensure no side-effects? (SRE + security follow-up).
- The dry-run test will need ephemeral credentials that are discoverable but not leakable in logs; tie to private replay infra ticket JIRA-PS-1984.
- Can routing policy surface be extended to show cost delta if fallback is used? Useful for finance visibility.

Immediate next steps / action items (owners):
- Diego: prototype Access Path list wireframe in Figma (due 2025-11-18).
- Priya: security review of fallback primitives and replay runner constraints (blocking decision; due 2025-11-14).
- Liam: backend contract sketch for rotation stepper (API endpoints + events) and sample payloads (due 2025-11-20).
- Maya (me): follow up with SRE on which logs/events can be replayed without side effects; add sandbox runner PO.

Notes to self / rough ideas to keep: 
- Consider a "impact estimate" microflow: before rotate/disable show an estimate of requests/hour and a likely number of affected downstream systems. Pull from last 72h activity.
- Mobile compact mode: show only status chips and critical actions (disable/rotate).
- Onboarding checklist for new org admins: encourage ephemeral svcaccts and 1-click test harness.

Risk / edge cases: 
- Large orgs with 1000s of keys: performance of Access Path list; need paginated, server-side grouping by owner and route.
- Legal/regulatory: don't allow auto-fallback where data residency or model variant constraints exist. Must check org policy before offering fallback.

Intended deliverables for grooming:
- Figma wires: Access Path list + Safe Rotate modal + Compact Audit timeline (priority 1)
- Small API contract PR (Liam) + example CLI command for rotation (priority 2)
- Security gating checklist for fallback and replay (priority 1)
- Small e2e smoke test harness + example sample request (priority 2)

If you're reviewing: quick calls to make: 
- Priya: confirm whether fallback is allowable for our high-compliance customers.
- SRE: confirm which events we can safely show masked tokens for.
- Solutions eng: any downstream customers who would need an "admin preview" email during rotation windows.

Random brainstorm notes (ignore if too noisy): 
- "Rotation templates" per integration type (terraform, k8s, helm, CI provider) — pick from common snippets.
- Small UX trick: show a micro-visual diff of role changes (expanded permissions vs trimmed ones).
- Consider a "dry-run webhook" that can be called by customers to validate their integration when a new key is created.

End. This is a working doc; push comments to this file or link PRs to JIRA-PS-1984 and CON-7421.
